articles.title: India's first virtual zoo opens in Indore with 14 | Akashvani News - Newsonair
articles.content: News On AIR | August 17, 2026 9:54 AM India’s first virtual zoo opens in Indore with 14-D cinema and virtual jungle safari facilities The country’s first virtual zoo has been started in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. Along with this, a 14-D cinema theatre and a virtual jungle safari have also been opened at the Indore Zoo. The 14-D cinema and virtual jungle safari have been developed under the PPP model at a cost of around Rs 4.5 crore. In the virtual jungle safari, people can experience forests and wildlife through technology. The 14-D cinema will offer visitors a different movie-watching experience. Yesterday, Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav inaugurated these facilities and also watched a film with school children in the 14-D cinema. These new facilities will help children and tourists learn about wildlife and nature through technology.

articles.title: Indore Gets India's First Virtual Zoo - GKToday
articles.content: Home Indore Gets India’s First Virtual Zoo Indore Gets India’s First Virtual Zoo August 17, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Indore in Madhya Pradesh has India’s first virtual zoo at the Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya, also known as the Indore Zoological Museum. The facility covers 8,000 square feet and was developed under a Public-Private Partnership model at an estimated cost of ₹4.5 crore. Virtual Zoo and Immersive Display Systems A virtual zoo is a technology-based attraction that uses digital projection, sound, motion, and special effects to simulate wildlife and forest environments. The Indore facility includes a 3-D dome theatre, a 14-D cinema, and a digital jungle safari for visitors. 14-D Cinema and Sensory Features The 14-D theatre integrates 14 sensory effects for an immersive viewing experience. These effects include synchronised moving seats, wind blasts, water sprays, fog, bubbles, and physical vibrations. Design Elements and Visitor Access The venue includes a gorilla-shaped entrance gate, neon-lit 3D jungle pathways, a fibre-optic glow garden, a roar-simulating maze, and a mirror bridge with a Hanuman hologram. The attraction opened to the public on 17 August 2026, and the entry ticket was fixed at ₹70 per person. Important Facts for Exams Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya is the zoological museum in Indore where the virtual zoo has been set up. Public-Private Partnership, or PPP, is a model in which a government body and a private entity share project responsibilities. 3-D dome theatres use a curved screen to create a wide field of view for viewers. 14-D cinema is a commercial entertainment format that combines visual projection with motion seats and environmental effects. Operational Details The virtual zoo operates from Tuesday to Sunday between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM. The venue conducts 16 shows daily, and each show lasts 20 minutes. articles.title: Indias First Sports AI Center Launches at LNIPE Gwalior | Tech Update
articles.content: English News Local Mp Gwalior Indias First Sports AI Center Launches At LNIPE Gwalior | Tech Update India’s first Sports AI Centre to open in Gwalior: AI to analyse athletes’ physique and suggest techniques to improve performance Arun More | Gwalior 19 hours ago Copy link The Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) in Gwalior is set to introduce Artificial Intelligence (AI) as part of its Sports Education Technology Upgradation initiative. The technology will not only help train athletes but also analyse their physical structure, movement and abilities in detail to identify areas for improvement. For example, if a high-jump athlete repeatedly falls short despite extensive training, AI-based physical analysis could identify the technical shortcomings. It could help determine the appropriate stride pattern, the point from which the athlete should take off and other aspects of the jump. The aim is to improve athletic performance and prepare players more effectively for national and international competitions. The centre is expected to be fully ready by November 2026. Early talent identification to become easier Gwalior is emerging as a hub for AI-based sports, education and agriculture, alongside its historical and cultural identity. LNIPE has launched the Sports Education Technology Upgradation initiative to modernise sports training at the institute. Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya has inaugurated a new Sports Science Block on the LNIPE campus, where the advanced AI Sports Centre is being developed. The centre will focus on early talent identification, athlete development and performance tracking using AI. Girls in shorts working out. Technology could prove a major boost for athletes Swimming athlete Homi Gupta said the AI project being introduced at LNIPE for swimming and other sports could take athletes’ fitness and performance to a new level. AI will make it easier to analyse postural deficiencies and movement patterns, helping coaches identify technical problems at an early stage. The technology could also help reduce the risk of injuries and enable athletes to improve their performance more quickly. AI-based analytics could identify complex performance issues and help athletes achieve better results in less time. 2 See pictures Machines are kept at LNIPE to check the bodies of players. Young players playing volleyball. Athletes will save time and energy Young athlete Ramji Sharma said the new AI and Sports Science Centre would be a major benefit for athletes like him. Earlier, athletes often had to travel to sports centres in major cities such as Delhi for fitness tests and advanced diagnostic assessments, costing them time and energy. With these facilities available at LNIPE, athletes will be able to assess their fitness accurately and regularly at the institute itself. Data generated through AI analysis could help athletes understand their weaknesses and scientifically improve their stamina and strength, helping them perform better at national and international competitions. AI could reshape the future of Indian sport The centre will work on talent identification, athlete development and long-term nurturing. articles.content: News cities bengaluru-news 'QR Codes Outside Hotels, Pharmacies For Food Complaints': Karnataka's First-In-India Push 'QR Codes Outside Hotels, Pharmacies For Food Complaints': Karnataka's First-In-India Push Reported By : Afreen Hussain , News18 Cities Edited By: Sumedha Kirti Last Updated: August 17, 2026, 12:51 IST Health Minister UT Khader announced QR codes outside hotels, pharmacies for food safety complaints, warned PG and hostel operators, and said notices have gone to 60 hotels so far. reset Rapid Read Rapid Read Summarized by AI. + More Rapid Read Like this summary? Share Your Feedback Health Minister UT Khader warned PG and hostel operators that they must maintain proper food standards. (AI image) Karnataka will introduce QR codes outside hotels and pharmacies allowing the public to scan and file food safety complaints directly, Health Minister UT Khader said, describing it as the first such initiative in the country. The announcement comes as the state’s Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) Department continues a wide-ranging crackdown on hygiene and quality violations across hotels, resorts and public food facilities. Khader said the QR code system would let members of the public scan a code outside hotels and pharmacies and submit complaints about problems or concerns on the spot, calling Karnataka the first state to roll out such a mechanism. He also announced plans for an International All India Food Safety Conclave, aimed at addressing what he described as inconsistencies in the quality and taste of products such as soft drinks sold in different countries. Central food safety regulations, he said, need to be strengthened so that standards in India match those followed elsewhere. What Warning Did He Issue To PG And Hostel Operators? Khader warned PG and hostel operators that they must maintain proper food standards, adding that there would be no leniency for establishments found serving poor-quality food. He said inspections would be extended beyond hotels to private hostels, bus stops, wedding halls, railway canteens and food served on flights. A dedicated watch team will be set up to strengthen food safety enforcement across these categories, he said. What Action Has Already Been Taken Against Hotels? On enforcement so far, Khader said notices had been issued to 60 hotels, of which 15 had responded. He added that the government would convene a meeting with hotel operators to discuss food safety concerns going forward. How Does This Fit Into Karnataka’s Wider Food Safety Crackdown? Khader’s announcement follows weeks of intensified inspections by the Karnataka FDA, which has reported seizing more than 1,000 kg of unsafe food items in recent operations statewide. articles.title: Karnataka To Introduce AI Education From Class 6, Chief Minister Announces AI Akshara ...
articles.content: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has announced the launch of the AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula programmes, aimed at introducing artificial intelligence and coding education in schools across the state. The initiatives are intended to equip students with skills needed to compete at the global level as technology continues to evolve. Speaking during his Independence Day address at the Field Marshal Manekshaw Parade Ground in Bengaluru, Shivakumar highlighted the changing technological landscape and said, “We are now entering a new technological era. The Al campaign and Coding Gurukula - this is your era, a new era,”. Under the new initiative, AI education will be introduced in Karnataka schools from Class 6 onwards. Shivakumar said the state government has already been working on programmes aimed at developing the skills of young people and preparing them to compete globally. “For this purpose, today I am announcing an important programme called the ‘AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula’,” he said. The Chief Minister also stressed the importance of improving the quality of education in schools and colleges so that students are better prepared for the emerging technology-driven era. AI University In Karnataka Proposed Karnataka is also moving ahead with plans to establish India’s first government-owned AI university in Bengaluru. Shivakumar said the government is working on the programme and noted the growing global interest in India’s artificial intelligence capabilities. “The entire world is looking at India for the country’s first government-owned Al university. I have already announced the establishment of an Al university in Bengaluru, Karnataka, and I am also formulating the programme,” he said. The proposal for an AI university was earlier announced by Shivakumar during Google I/O Connect India 2026 in July. At the event, he had also said that AI learning would be introduced for students from Class 6. The announcements come ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, scheduled to be held from November 17 to November 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC). The proposed initiatives are part of Karnataka’s wider efforts to strengthen technology education and prepare its youth for the changing demands of the global workforce.

articles.title: India's 1st Virtual Zoo Lets You Experience The Jungle In 14D Without Leaving Your Seat
articles.content: Home / India / Trending / India’s 1st Virtual Zoo Lets You Experience The Jungle In 14D Without Leaving Your Seat The virtual zoo initiative in Indore will help provide accessible wildlife learning through digital technology, advance environmental conservation education and also boost footfall at the zoo! by Ashmeet Guliani Updated: August 17, 2026 12:30 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Indore Municipal Corporation/X and Canva Pro/Tima Miroshnichenko Good News! Indore in Madhya Pradesh is now home to India’s first virtual zoo, where visitors can experience a realistic wild jungle without even leaving their seats. The theatre with a 14D screen will make you feel as if you are actually inside the forest with the animals. Curious to know more about this? Read on! Indore Gets India’s First Virtual Zoo Travellers, you now have another reason to visit Indore in Madhya Pradesh . The city now has the country’s first 14D Virtual Zoo along with a Digital Jungle Safari at Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya. According to The Times of India, this zoo and safari were inaugurated by MP’s Chief Minister Mohan Yadav. It was constructed at a cost of ₹4.6 crore under a PPP model. The 8,000-square-foot facility is now open to the public. It features a 14D cinema theatre with a waterproof screen imported from South Korea, a digital jungle safari and a 3D dome theatre. Visitors will get to experience 14 real-life effects like water sprays, wind blasts, fog, bubbles, smells and moving seats to match the action on the screen. These sensory experiences will make you feel as if you are actually inside a jungle instead of in a theatre. Also Read: Gujarat To Get Asia’s 1st Desert-Themed Night Safari & Zoo; Here’s What Wildlife Lovers Can Expect This Virtual Zoo Has A Gorilla-Shaped Door! Here comes the best part. The theatre has a giant door shaped like a gorilla’s mouth! It is so cool, right? Not just that, the facility also has neon-lit 3D jungle pathways. According to The Times of India, the theatre will run from Tuesday to Sunday, from 10 am to 6 pm. It will host 16 shows daily, with each show lasting 20 minutes. To get this jungle experience at Indore Zoo, visitors will have to pay ₹70 to access all three attractions. The virtual zoo initiative, executed by Indore Municipal Corporation, has many advantages. It will help provide accessible wildlife learning through digital technology, advance environmental conservation education and also boost footfall at the zoo! articles.title: CM Revanth Reddy to inaugurate AI -equipped Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS today
articles.content: News On AIR | August 17, 2026 6:18 AM CM Revanth Reddy to inaugurate AI-equipped Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS today Chief Minister Revanth Reddy will inaugurate Dr. Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS, Telangana’s new super-specialty hospital in Sanathnagar today. Built to bring corporate-level healthcare to common people, it is the largest super-specialty hospital built in a single phase in the government sector, spread over 22.6 acres. The hospital has 1,082 beds, including 300 ICU beds, 31 major and 6 minor operation theatres, and advanced diagnostic labs. It is India’s first government hospital to install an AI-based pneumatic tube system, which moves blood samples and medical reports between wards, labs, and pharmacy in just one to two minutes. TIMS is designated a Centre of Excellence in six areas.. organ transplants, cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, nephrology, and trauma care. It has advanced imaging equipment. The hospital achieved IGBC Gold rating for saving 75 percent water through sustainable design. Ahead of the inauguration, Health Minister Damodar Rajanarsimha reviewed arrangements on Sunday with officials from Health, Police, GHMC, Traffic, and Water Board departments, directing them to ensure smooth entry, parking, security, sanitation, and water and power supply for the event.

articles.title: How Karnataka will create 1 lakh new jobs - HR Katha
articles.content: Share LinkedIn Twitter Facebook WhatsApp Karnataka Chief Minister has announced plans to create one lakh new jobs, expand AI education and build technology hubs across the State as part of the government’s vision for a “Young Karnataka–New India”. Speaking at his Independence Day address in Bengaluru on 15 August, Shivakumar announced the Udyoga Sankalpa and Udyoga Nidhi schemes to boost employment and entrepreneurship. He revealed that the government is also working to fill 72,000 key vacancies, with notifications for these posts expected within six months. Under Udyoga Nidhi, entrepreneurs in 10 economically-backward districts will receive Rs 2,500 per month for every new job created, with a target of one lakh additional jobs. Artificial intelligence (AI) will be introduced in government schools from Class 6, along with the proposed AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula programmes. Bengaluru will get India’s first government-owned AI university, while AI hubs will support the technology ecosystem. Five global technology centres are proposed in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru. An Advanced Manufacturing Cluster in Doddaballapura has attracted Rs 20,000 crore in investment commitments and could create around one lakh jobs. The State is targeting a $3 trillion economy by 2047. It will also use drones and satellite images for crop surveys, while small farmers will get a 50 per cent subsidy on machinery rentals. Karnataka also plans major infrastructure expansion, including 220 km of Metro in Bengaluru, a 117-km ring road and 7,100 km of rural roads. Water security projects worth Rs 16,000 crore have been approved. The government has proposed a state-owned Motor Vehicle Insurance Corporation to simplify insurance and speed up claims. Bengaluru’s police commissionerate will also be divided into five units. Meanwhile, BJP leader R Ashok has sought a white paper on welfare schemes, alleging differences between the latest figures and earlier government data on Shakti and Gruha Lakshmi. articles.title: Delhi Witnesses North India's First Indoor Tennis Facility - Sports News Portal | Revsportz
articles.content: Share Facebook Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Pinterest Email PC: Facebook (Ethical Tennis Academy) Tennis players in Delhi will no longer have to allow the weather to dictate their training schedules, with the introduction of the Ethical Tennis Academy in Dwarka, North India’s first indoor tennis facility. The academy has two fully covered clay courts, allowing players to train and play throughout the year without having to contend with the capital’s often challenging weather conditions.Alongside this, the facility has a five-stage player development pathway and high-performance training facilities, giving players greater consistency in their training schedules. Considering Delhi’s extreme summer heat, monsoon rains and periods of poor air quality that have traditionally made uninterrupted outdoor training difficult, this academy ensures that the courts are open and playable 365 days a year, making it one of the few options in the region where tennis can continue without weather-related interruptions. The development also comes at a time when tennis infrastructure in the country is gradually expanding beyond conventional outdoor courts. The academy offers coaching for all age groups and pay-and-play options for adults or casual players, and it is helmed by former tennis professional Kshitij Kamal, Director of Ethical Tennis Academy. The Dwarka facility could help address the existing gaps by providing players with access to clay-court training in a controlled environment throughout the year. Ethical Tennis Academy

articles.title: Karnataka CM Announces AI Akshara Abhiyana, Coding Gurukula for School Students from Class 6
articles.content: The Chief Minister of Karnataka, D K Shivakumar, has announced a state-wide programme aimed at bringing artificial intelligence (AI) and coding education to school students. The initiative, called AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula, was announced during his Independence Day address in Bengaluru on August 15. According to a PTI report, AI education will be introduced in schools from Class 6 onwards, as part of the programme. The initiative aims to help students develop technology-related skills and prepare them for emerging opportunities in the global economy. Government Plans AI University in Bengaluru Shivakumar also said his government was working to establish India's first government-owned AI University in Bengaluru. Stressing on the need to improve the quality of schools and colleges, the CM said an expert committee constituted to reform the examination system would submit its report within two months. The CM said that the government is also working on a proposal to establish a government-owned AI University in Bengaluru and highlighted the need for reforms in the education system. He also stressed that an expert committee constituted to examine changes to the examination system is expected to submit its recommendations within two months. The state government's education and youth-focused plans are part of its broader “Youth Karnataka, New India” vision. Focus on Youth Employment and Rural Students Alongside the AI education initiative, Shivakumar announced several measures focused on employment and skill development. The government plans to fill approximately 72,000 vacancies in government departments within six months. The state will also introduce Udyoga Sethu, aimed at helping job seekers connect with opportunities in the private sector. Industries generating new employment will be eligible for an incentive of approximately Rs 2,500 per job per month for two years, with the programme expected to cover up to one lakh jobs. For students from rural government schools, the government plans to implement the Sahaya Hasta/Hosa Hasta scheme and provide 7.5 per cent reservation in professional higher education, including courses in medicine and engineering. Karnataka's Technology and Development Push The Chief Minister also outlined Karnataka's broader development plans, including a target of taking the state's economy to USD 3 trillion by 2047. The government is simultaneously focusing on technology-led agriculture. Under the proposed Raitha Chaitanya scheme, drones, satellite technology and real-time data will be used for crop insurance surveys and information related to agricultural pests, diseases and markets. Several infrastructure, healthcare, water security and urban development projects were also highlighted during the Independence Day address.
